title: DF-SQD: Deterministic Fields for Sampling-Based Quantum Diagonalization
abstract: Sampling-based quantum diagonalization method exploits Quantum-centric supercomputing platforms to sample bitstrings for Hamiltonian projection on a quantum computer, and then classically diagonalize the Hamiltonian to estimate the eigenvalues and eigenvectors. In current quantum devices an algorithm is useful when shallow quantum circuits with error mitigation support can discover better results while having either a proof of convergence or some method to explain trust in experiment. In this paper, we introduce DF-SQD, a hybrid algorithm that derives deterministic auxiliary-field circuits from selected double-factorization leaves of the two-electron tensor. The circuits propose occupation-number configurations, while selected configuration interaction evaluates the original active-space Hamiltonian and can recentre subsequent proposal rounds. On N2 (32 qubits; 6-31G basis) and a 40-qubit [Fe2S2(SCH3)4]2- active-space Hamiltonian, we show that DF-SQD improves the energy obtained from sampled determinant spaces while using shallow number-preserving circuits in both simulator and hardware runs. For N2, DF-SQD is 45x more accurate with a 11.23\% smaller subspace, and due to its ability to sample better bitstrings at lesser shots it is 2.93x faster than SQD in quantum devices. For the iron-sulfur cluster, DF-SQD generated a subspace dimension of 221M with 400K shots, while SQD needed 1.5M shots to generate a 238M subspace, thus we have better subspace recovery evident from the hardware at 3.75x reduced shots. At a matched 50M subspace dimension, DF-SQD is 1.32x more accurate (achieves a 24.5\% relative error reduction over standard SQD). So overall, our method is able to discover better results with shallower circuits, is sample efficient, uses configuration recovery (so has targeted error mitigation) and we have empirical convergence observation.
summary: This paper introduces DF-SQD, a novel hybrid quantum-classical algorithm designed to improve the sampling-based diagonalization of molecular Hamiltonians. By deriving deterministic auxiliary-field circuits, DF-SQD efficiently proposes quantum states, leading to superior energy accuracy and reduced resource requirements compared to prior methods on benchmark molecules like $	ext{N}_2$ and $	ext{Fe}_2	ext{S}_2$.
main_problem: The core problem is the quantum diagonalization of the Hamiltonian to accurately estimate ground-state eigenvalues and eigenvectors in quantum chemistry, which is computationally intractable for large systems.
main_result: The proposed DF-SQD method significantly improves energy accuracy and resource efficiency compared to existing sampling-based methods (SQD) on both small ($	ext{N}_2$) and larger ($	ext{Fe}_2	ext{S}_2$) molecular systems.
method: DF-SQD is a hybrid algorithm that uses quantum circuits to deterministically propose occupation-number configurations, followed by classical configuration interaction to evaluate the Hamiltonian and guide subsequent proposals.
model_or_system: The work applies to quantum chemistry calculations, specifically simulating the $	ext{N}_2$ molecule and the $	ext{Fe}_2	ext{S}_2$ cluster, utilizing active-space Hamiltonians and mapping them onto qubit systems.
key_observables: Energy error (relative to reference calculations), selected product-space dimension (number of determinants), sampling time, and QPU usage.
important_parameters: Active space size (e.g., 32 qubits for $	ext{N}_2$, 40 qubits for $	ext{Fe}_2	ext{S}_2$), number of shots, and error tolerances.
main_assumptions: The method relies on the ability to derive deterministic auxiliary-field circuits and assumes that the energy estimate converges monotonically with increasing sampling resources.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the workflow (DF-SQD schematic), and comparisons of energy error and product-space dimension between DF-SQD and SQD on $	ext{N}_2$ and $	ext{Fe}_2	ext{S}_2$ using both simulation and hardware results.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the DF-SQD hybrid algorithm, details its mechanism using auxiliary-field circuits, and validates its performance by comparing it against established sampling methods on two distinct molecular systems ($	ext{N}_2$ and $	ext{Fe}_2	ext{S}_2$) across simulation and hardware platforms.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the resource scaling challenge in quantum chemistry simulations, providing a concrete, hybrid algorithmic improvement for accessing high-accuracy electronic structure data on near-term quantum hardware.
